The public officers of the Mandokoro were herded together into the diagonal-front <ruby>viewing section<rt>kensho</rt></ruby>. A pillar stood in the way. For enjoying Noh it was the worst seat in the house, and for people of our standing, exactly the correct one.

The senior officials, the main guests, had not arrived yet. But a large man who looked like Doushin Yusa was already there. Such promptness was unusual for someone of his position. Perhaps he was being a considerate host.

As always, the Kubo wore a stylish <ruby>hitatare<rt>hitatare</rt></ruby>. Today, though, a navy hood had been added on top. What was that meant to signify?

en.html:
Even after the officials and their families had taken their seats, the main seat in the center-front remained empty. Who would sit there, we all knew.

Soon a party of rather heavy appearance came in. The weight came less from the man at its head than from the ladies-in-waiting and guards packed around him. They moved toward that seat.

Shirou Kuniuji Ashikaga.

The boy who would inherit the post of Lord General of the Six Guards from his dead grandfather, and become head of Rokuhara. No, head of the whole realm.

He walked quietly, with no great pleasure on his face. Then suddenly he turned his head, as if he had felt a gaze of a different kind.

He looked in one direction.

...Sakurako Okabe.

The boy's eyes opened wide in surprise. Like anyone else, he had not expected to see her at this gathering.

He blinked to check, and looked again. And the surprise turned into joy he could not hold back.

He had noticed the small ornament decorating the princess: one flower, from the ones he had sent her.

Princess Sakurako returned his gaze with a small smile.

With a crowd between them, an invisible thread had definitely been tied.

ja.html:
一通り高官やその妻子らが座に着いた後も、正面の
中央、主賓の席はまだ空いたままだった。
　誰がそこへ着くのかはわかっている。

　程なく。
　一際物々しい集団――それは集団の頭たる人物より
周りを固める女官や警護兵によるところが大きかった
――が現れて、その主賓席へ向かう。

　足利四郎邦氏である。
　やがて六衛大将領の地位を死せる祖父から受け継ぎ、
六波羅の……否、天下の棟梁となるべき少年。

　さして心楽しくもなさそうに静々と歩く彼は、ふと、
唐突に顔の向きを変えた。
　何か、種類の異なる視線を感じ取ったかのように。

　一方向を見る。
　……岡部桜子。

　少年の眼が驚きに見開かれた。
　誰もがそうであろうが、この会でその姿を見るとは
思わなかったのだろう。

　確認する風で瞼を瞬かせ、改めて見直す。
　そして、驚きの表情は抑え難い喜びに変じた。

　姫の容姿を彩る、ささやかな装飾を見て取ったのだ。
　彼が贈り届けた花――その一輪。

　少年の眼差しに、桜子姫が小さく笑みを返す。
　
　人垣を隔てて、見えざる糸が確かに繋がった。

en.html:
I did not claim any special understanding of Noh. Still, I could recognize the performer's extraordinary skill.

In every move of the dance there was dignity. A <ruby>warrior<rt>warrior</rt></ruby>'s spirit <ruby>overflowed<rt>overflowed</rt></ruby> in each sweep of the fan.

Above all, the voice. It was a whole class apart from mere good singing.

Feeling.

The principal actor's lines had living feeling inside their artistic intonation.

The sorrow of a warrior fated to defeat was sung in a <ruby>melody<rt>melody</rt></ruby> of the most beautiful kind.

This rare combination could only be a master's craft.

From the look of him, the <ruby>Zaou<rt>Zaou</rt></ruby> school of the Kongou line, perhaps...

en.html:
The second half of Yorimasa is mainly about describing the battle as Yorimasa tells it. There is not much portrayal of the hero's mind, the very thing that makes a tragedy tragic.

Yet it seemed to reach us anyway.

Why had the man Yorimasa Minamoto been forced to fight? What had he been thinking when he fought?

His anguish.

His grief.

In each movement of the actor, the whole of one human being lived.

—I could <ruby>see<rt>see</rt></ruby> it.

A warrior who had the wings of sword-armor, yet chose to step into the river with his soldiers and raise their courage: a man of great nerve.

The Noh stage <ruby>is not<rt>is not</rt></ruby> a stage. It is one world.

Some people say this. When the actor's power is more than enough, it is perfectly true.

The stage had become another world.

The Uji River of seven hundred and sixty years ago was there.

—Or perhaps Inawashiro in Aizu, only last month.

――<ruby>視<rt>み</rt></ruby>える。
　劒冑という翼を持つ武者の身でありながら、敢えて
兵と共に川へ踏み込むを選び、味方を大いに鼓舞する
豪胆な男の姿が。

　能の舞台は舞台に<ruby>非<rt>あら</rt></ruby>ず。
　一つの世界である。

　そう云う者がいる。
　能楽師の力量が充分以上であるとき、それは完全に
正しい。

　いまや舞台は別世界であった。
　七六〇年前の宇治川がそこにある。

　――あるいは、つい先月の会津猪苗代が。

《'Where the water churns backward, know that rocks are there.
Put weak horses downstream, and let strong ones block the water.》

《Give the <ruby>ends of bows<rt>ends of bows</rt></ruby> to those who are swept away,
and join your strength, one with another.'》

《By the order of one man alone,
though the river was so great, not one rider was lost before reaching this bank.》

The last stronghold, the one he had taken as his final shield, was broken.

The enemy, in high spirit, rushed into the allied lines like a flood.

Comrades were killed one after another. Among them was the kin he had trusted most.

The old general was alone now.

せよ》
《流れん武者には<ruby>弓弭<rt>ゆはず</rt></ruby>を取らせ、
　互いに力を合はすべしと》
《唯一人の下知によって……
　さばかりの大河なれども一騎も流れず此方
の岸に》

　最後の盾とした要害も破られて。
　勢いづく敵軍は味方の陣に怒涛と攻め入る。

　次々と殺されてゆく同胞……
　その中には何より頼りとした肉親もいる。

　老将はもはや一人。

On the grass, he spread his fan.

He threw off his armor, sat down, and drew his sword.

Then he sang his death poem, one last verse.

Then he sang his death poem, one last verse.

ja.html:
芝の上に、扇を敷き。
　鎧を脱ぎ捨てて座り、刀を抜く。

　そうして、歌う――
　辞世の一句を。
ja.text:
芝の上に、扇を敷き。
　鎧を脱ぎ捨てて座り、刀を抜く。

　そうして、歌う――
　辞世の一句を。

en.html:
《This <ruby>buried tree<rt>buried tree</rt></ruby> never bloomed with flowers,
and how pitiful, the end my body has come to.》

　身のなる果ては哀れなりけり》

《埋木うもれぎの花咲く事もなかりしに

en.html:
—He had known the flower would never bloom.

Still, there was no other way but to stand and end like this, and he only pitied himself for it.

　それでも立ち上がり、こうして果てるほかなかった
己を哀れむばかりだ。

en.html:
'Yorimasa' went away.

The traveling monk's dream ended.

Quietly, to the last, the performance drew to a close... Only the low sobbing of a daughter who had lost her father shook the air of the Noh hall.
